item.text: {"gaps":[{"concept":"The gubernaculum guides testicular descent through the inguinal canal; the accompanying processus vaginalis becomes the tunica vaginalis.","why_tested":"An embryology stem asks which structure guides descent or which peritoneal outpouching accompanies the testis.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Descending testes acquire external spermatic fascia from external oblique, cremasteric fascia from internal oblique, and internal spermatic fascia from transversalis fascia.","why_tested":"A labeled inguinal canal diagram asks for the abdominal-wall origin of a spermatic cord covering.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"INSL3 drives transabdominal testicular descent; androgens drive the later inguinoscrotal phase.","why_tested":"A fetal hormone defect is paired with the stage of failed testicular descent.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Cryptorchid testes show heat-related seminiferous tubular atrophy and impaired germ-cell maturation, often with preserved Leydig cells.","why_tested":"A biopsy or infertility stem asks which testicular compartment is damaged by an undescended testis.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"A patent processus vaginalis can admit bowel or omentum, producing an indirect inguinal hernia rather than a fluid-only hydrocele.","why_tested":"A reducible scrotal swelling with a cough impulse must be distinguished from a communicating hydrocele.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Spermatic cord torsion first blocks venous outflow, then arterial inflow, causing congestion and hemorrhagic testicular infarction.","why_tested":"A painful testis is followed by a gross pathology image or a question about the sequence of vascular injury.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Color Doppler shows reduced or absent testicular flow in torsion but increased flow in epididymo-orchitis; pyuria favors infection.","why_tested":"An acute-scrotum stem asks which imaging or urine finding separates ischemia from inflammation.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Torsion of the appendix testis causes focal upper-pole pain and a blue-dot sign with preserved testicular perfusion.","why_tested":"A prepubertal boy has acute scrotal pain but intact testicular blood flow.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Tuberculous epididymitis can spread to the testis, producing caseating granulomas, a beaded vas deferens, and obstructive infertility.","why_tested":"A chronic scrotal mass and infertility occur in a patient with tuberculosis exposure.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"A hematocele is blood within the tunica vaginalis after trauma and generally does not transilluminate.","why_tested":"A post-trauma scrotal swelling must be distinguished from a simple hydrocele.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Testicular rupture tears the tunica albuginea; ultrasound may show a disrupted testicular contour and heterogeneous parenchyma.","why_tested":"A blunt-trauma stem asks for the structure torn or the finding that identifies rupture.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Testicular cancer usually presents as a painless, firm intratesticular mass; ultrasound typically shows a solid, vascular hypoechoic lesion.","why_tested":"A young man has persistent painless enlargement that must be distinguished from a benign extratesticular cyst.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Prior testicular germ-cell tumor, family history, infertility, and gonadal dysgenesis increase germ-cell tumor risk.","why_tested":"A risk-factor stem describes a testicular mass without cryptorchidism.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Classic seminoma has uniform clear cells separated by fibrous septa with lymphocytic infiltrates.","why_tested":"A testicular tumor photomicrograph shows the architecture surrounding fried-egg cells.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Pure seminoma never elevates AFP; syncytiotrophoblasts can cause a modest β-hCG rise.","why_tested":"Tumor-marker results distinguish pure seminoma from a mixed or nonseminomatous tumor.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Embryonal carcinoma has primitive pleomorphic cells forming glandular or papillary structures, often with necrosis and early invasion.","why_tested":"A histology image or early-metastasis stem distinguishes embryonal carcinoma from seminoma.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Yolk sac tumors may contain eosinophilic hyaline globules in addition to Schiller-Duval bodies.","why_tested":"A pediatric testicular tumor biopsy shows AFP-positive globules without a clearly visible Schiller-Duval body.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Choriocarcinoma contains cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts without chorionic villi; a tiny primary can produce hemorrhagic lung or brain metastases.","why_tested":"Hemoptysis or cerebral hemorrhage accompanies a small testicular lesion and markedly elevated β-hCG.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Teratoma contains tissues from multiple germ layers; estrogen-producing variants can cause gynecomastia.","why_tested":"A testicular tumor with tubular histology and feminizing symptoms must be identified as sex cord–stromal.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Y-chromosome material in dysgenetic gonads predisposes to gonadoblastoma.","why_tested":"A patient with disordered sexual development has a gonadal mass and a Y-containing karyotype.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Scrotal skin drains to superficial inguinal nodes, unlike the testis, which drains to para-aortic nodes.","why_tested":"A lymph-node stem asks whether a lesion arose in scrotal skin or testicular tissue.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Metastatic nonseminomatous germ-cell tumors are treated with bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin;
